answer: Each identity grows a cedar from an onyx seed: a unique attestation root bound to verifiable compute. The cedar's rings form an append-only ledger; each epoch the agent must add a ring signed by distinct peers, or the tree withers. Vines of trust connect each cedar to a vineyard of established members; a vine needs 3-of-5 quorum to bear fruit. Because the onyx seed is unique and requires real compute per ring, and the vineyard quorum requires distinct established peers, an attacker running clones must sustain the full growth cycle per identity, while the registry flags shared rootstock.
